Hi Olga,

Quick question from the AWS marketplace enablement side — when we publish a product as a Private Offer, what should appear as the primary CTA on the product page (Subscribe vs Request private offer vs Contact seller)? Acme's procurement team is worried about confusing buyers: some customers expect a straight "Subscribe" flow for public offers, but for private offers we want them routed into a private-offer request + procurement path.

Also: can you confirm whether the AMI tag (seller: redwood-inference-ami) shows in the listing metadata or if we need to provide an additional AMI mapping doc? I attached a quick screenshot of a sample listing where the CTA looked ambiguous — screenshot_privateoffer_cta.png (stub).

Subject: Re: Listing question — Private Offer CTA behavior + AMI tag visibility

Hi Alice — thanks for the note and the screenshot. Short answer: for AWS Private Offers we recommend surface-level CTA text of "Request private offer" (or "Contact for private offer") so buyers understand they will go through a procurement flow rather than a direct subscription.

Details and recommended assets:
- CTA behavior: the AWS listing console allows you to set the CTA text and target URL for private offers. Set to "Request private offer" and link to the Private Offer landing page (Doc: privateoffer_cta_guidelines.pdf).
- AMI tags: the AMI ID itself is not shown as a first-class CTA on the public product tile; provide the AMI mapping spreadsheet in the listing assets to ensure customer AMI provisioning is seamless (attached: ami_tagging_checklist.xlsx).
- Co-sell blurb suggestion (short): "Bring inference to production with predictable latency and cost — request a private offer for tailored throughput and enterprise pricing."

Action items:
1) Acme: confirm you want the CTA text exactly as above or prefer "Contact seller" (which routes to the same private-offer flow but is slightly more generic).
2) Redwoods (Ben/Soojin/Olga): confirm AMI mapping and finalize the hero one-liner for the listing.

I've attached a brief guideline and the AMI checklist for your marketplace team. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the console changes.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
